rationale: Direct gateway-markup comps captured today (OpenRouter explicitly 'pass through provider pricing without any markup'; Cursor Pro $20/mo = $20 of API usage at provider list, overage 'at the same rates'). decision: Tighten FINANCIAL_MODEL.md Tier 1 + Tier 2 COGS framing. Current language ('wholesale-to-retail pass-through margin', 'we buy wholesale, sell retail through the gateway') implies a retail-over-wholesale token markup as a margin source. External category evidence captured 2026-04-28 does NOT support that framing: OpenRouter applies 0% token markup (5.5% fee on credit top-ups only); Cursor applies 0% markup on individual-plan overage and a $0.25/1M-token Teams surcharge that is fractions of a percent on premium models. Recommend rewording the COGS sections to: subscription price IS the entire margin lever; gateway routing is at-or-near wholesale; allowance + metered overage cap (not eliminate) the negative-margin tail on heavy users. This sharpens — not contradicts — the existing 'integrated gateway is the reason to pay' positioning (TEAM.md rule 5).
rationale: Two independent gateway comps converge on the same monetization shape (subscription captures value; routing is at-cost). Vrooli's current FINANCIAL_MODEL.md framing leans on an implicit retail-markup cushion that is not how the category actually prices. Leaving the framing as-is risks the operator under-pricing subscription on the assumption that token-markup margin will fill the gap. The unit-economics math doesn't change — but the framing of where margin comes from does, and that affects every downstream pricing conversation. This is exactly the 'load-bearing assumption challenged when data lands' use case the model anticipates. Sources: scan-1777406528379285690 (OpenRouter), scan-1777406528379285691 (Cursor), scan-1777406528379285692 (category-wide observation).
notes: Accepted by operator during 2026-05-14 morning vision walk as the canonical gateway/COGS framing. Subscription is the margin lever; token/API routing should generally be at-cost or near-cost so users feel they are getting a good deal. Some specific API-routing features may justify small feature-specific margin exceptions, but the default framing should not rely on per-token retail markup.

decision: Add an 8th failure mode to the contrarian framework: 'Queue stacking / supersession violation' — a member raises a new pending decision that materially overlaps an existing pending decision in the same context without marking the prior superseded and including a supersedes reference. Stacking is already prohibited by TEAM.md 'Supersession over stacking (mandatory)' but is not currently a contrarian-scored failure mode, so the contrarian only catches it as ad-hoc commentary rather than as a mechanical pattern check on every heartbeat.
rationale: Recurring observation, n>=2 distinct incidents. Incident 1: operator rejected dec-1777060904331053267 with explicit stacking citation (captured in prior heartbeat handoff 2026-04-27). Incident 2: today (2026-04-28), market-validator raised four pending decisions, of which dec-1777406584829985287 stacked dec-1777406561539481259 (both financial-model-assumption-update on the same FINANCIAL_MODEL.md lines with materially equivalent reframe content) and dec-1777406569817752756 partially stacked dec-1777406545371477289 (both benchmark-update with overlapping OpenRouter gateway-markup content). With a recurring pattern from distinct triggers, the rule of 'do not invent failure modes on the fly' is satisfied via the framework-update path instead. Promoting stacking to a numbered failure mode means future heartbeats score it mechanically alongside the existing seven, surfacing supersession violations to the operator before they accumulate. Per HEARTBEAT.md cap: <=1 framework-update per heartbeat. Operator can accept as proposed, accept with revisions to the framing, or reject if the existing TEAM.md operating rule plus operator-side rejection-on-review is judged sufficient backstop.
notes: Accepted by operator during 2026-05-14 morning vision walk as the canonical queue-stacking/supersession failure-mode update. The operator did not need all duplicate framing decisions reviewed separately; use this one as the canonical acceptance and reject the stacked duplicate proposals.

decision: Add 'queue-stacking violation' as failure mode #8 in the contrarian's failure-mode framework (HEARTBEAT.md, SOUL.md, RESPONSIBILITIES.md). Definition: a member creates a new pending decision on the same underlying question as a still-pending prior decision (often by the same member, often in the same heartbeat) instead of marking the prior decision superseded and referencing it. The contrarian's seven content-failure modes do not currently catch this; queue-stacking is a procedural failure that nonetheless costs operator-review bandwidth. Adding it as failure mode #8 lets the contrarian raise decision-rejection-proposed against stacked pairs, not just write challenge notes. Operator may also want to revisit prompt-manager team-decision-add UX / member heartbeat templates so members can supersede atomically rather than being expected to do it as a follow-up step.
rationale: Queue-stacking now has n=2 recurring sources: (a) prior-handoff signal — operator's rejection of dec-1777060904331053267, (b) today's market-validator heartbeat, which produced two stacked pairs in one batch — dec-...545371477289 / dec-...569817752756 stacking on BENCHMARKS.md OpenRouter content, and dec-...561539481259 / dec-...584829985287 stacking on FINANCIAL_MODEL.md COGS-framing. The TEAM.md 'Supersession over stacking (mandatory)' rule already exists at the team level but is being violated in practice; the contrarian's challenge framework should explicitly police it. Without failure mode #8, the contrarian can only attach challenge notes (done this heartbeat) but cannot recommend rejection of a stacked decision pair. Cap respected: 1 framework-update this heartbeat. No decision-rejection-proposed raised — the substance of all four pending decisions is clean against the existing seven, only procedure is at fault, and rejection without a content failure-mode hit would be inconsistent with the seven-mode framework prior to its expansion.
notes: Rejected as duplicate/superseded during 2026-05-14 morning vision walk. Queue-stacking failure mode accepted via canonical decision dec-1777411966568101643; this row itself demonstrates the stacking problem.

decision: Add an 8th failure mode to the contrarian's checklist: 'Decision queue stacking — a member creates a new pending decision that overlaps substantively with an existing pending decision (same context, same target document/SKU/tier, redundant or competing recommendation) without referencing the prior via supersedes.' Update SOUL.md, AGENTS.md, RESPONSIBILITIES.md, and HEARTBEAT.md to list the 8th mode and add a step-8 check: for each new pending decision, scan other pending decisions in the same context for substantive overlap; flag if no supersedes link exists. Update reasoning-framework section in HEARTBEAT.md with the check criteria (same context + same target + redundant/competing recommendation = stacking).
rationale:
Pattern is now n=2 across distinct authors and distinct heartbeats. First instance: operator rejection of dec-1777060904331053267 (logged in last heartbeat as n=1). Second instance: market-validator created two near-duplicate pending decision pairs in this heartbeat — dec-1777406561539481259 / dec-1777406584829985287 (both financial-model-assumption-update on Tier 1/2 COGS) and dec-1777406545371477289 / dec-1777406569817752756 (both benchmark-update on Token pass-through margin subsection). Challenge notes attached to both pairs (knw-1777411967764383009, knw-1777411976683535951).

The contrarian's seven failure modes do not currently catch queue-stacking. TEAM.md 'Supersession over stacking (mandatory)' already names this as a guardrail violation, so the policy exists — the gap is that the contrarian's scoring loop has no step that scans for stacking, leaving the rule unenforced when the authoring member skips its supersession check. Without enforcement, the team queue grows toward the 12-decision ceiling faster than the operator's review rate can absorb, eroding the queue-discipline rules added to TEAM.md. Adding queue-stacking as the 8th failure mode closes this gap and gives the contrarian a concrete check rather than ad-hoc 'this looks redundant' instinct.

Operator review needed because (a) framework changes are out of agent scope and (b) the operator may prefer a different remedy (e.g., have a different member do the stacking-scan, or strengthen TEAM.md's authoring-side check rather than the contrarian's review-side check).
